text: US stocks slipped Friday, led by a second straight drop in tech. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,562, the Nasdaq fell 0.9% and the Dow edged up 0.1%. Nvidia fell again after its CEO resigned, and Treasury yields rose. Most sectors outside tech finished higher, and the S&P 500 still gained 2.5% on the week, its first winning week since early October. The TSX was steadier, closing at 36,106, down 0.1%. Globally, Europe held flat at a record while Asia mostly fell, with Hong Kong tech hit hardest.
mood: Cautious, not panicked: the worry is concentrated in AI and tech, and the rest of the market held up.

veqt.t: Down on the day: S&P 500 -0.4%, Nasdaq -0.9%, Dow +0.1%. Still up 2.5% on the week.
Mixed to flat. Europe was unchanged at a record (STOXX 600 +0.02%, FTSE +0.4%, DAX -0.1%). Japan rose 0.5%, Australia fell 0.7%.
The weakest sleeve. Hong Kong -1.6% (tech index -3%), Korea -1.0%, Shanghai -0.6%, India -0.6%. Taiwan rose about 1.4%.

label: Slightly bearish today
